aarti.tek: The service of Gaṇapati is an auspicious reward; by service all obstacles are averted. All the gods of the three worlds stand at his door and ever make their petition.
aarti.pad1: Ṛddhi and Siddhi sit on his right and left, and wave the fly-whisk with joy. Holding incense, lamps and the āratī, the devotees stand and raise the cry of victory. ॥1॥
aarti.pad2: Modakas of jaggery are offered to him; mounted on his mouse, he goes about. Seeing Gaṇapati's gentle form, obstacles run and fall far away. ॥2॥
aarti.pad3: In the month of Bhādoṃ, on the fourth day of the bright fortnight, at midday, obstacles fell far away: Lord Gaṇapati was born, and Durgā's heart filled with joy. ॥3॥
aarti.pad4: Indra's wondrous music sounded; the gods and kinsfolk all sang. Joy welled up in Śrī Śiva; on hearing Gaṇapati's name, all obstacles are averted. ॥4॥
aarti.pad5: Brahmā the Creator came and took his seat; Indra's apsarases danced. Brahmā looked into the Veda and named him Vighnavināśaka, destroyer of obstacles. ॥5॥
aarti.pad6: The one-tusked, elephant-faced Vināyaka bears a three-eyed form beyond compare. His legs are like pillars and his belly is full; the Moon-god laughed at him. ॥6॥
aarti.pad7: He cursed Śrī Candra and at once stripped him of his digits. Gaṇapati roams the fourteen worlds and reigns over the three worlds. ॥7॥
aarti.pad8: Whoever rises at dawn and does japa and meditation, all his works are accomplished. Whoever sings the āratī at the time of worship, the canopy of fame is waved over his head. ॥8॥
aarti.pad9: By worshipping Gaṇapati first, all works are accomplished without hindrance. All the devotees of Gaṇapati praise him with folded hands. ॥9॥
